title: NASA Human Research Program: ongoing research in space
challenge_note: Articles on ongoing Human Research Program research.

groups.name: Human investigations in low Earth orbit

studies.name: ARCHeR
studies.summary: Artemis Research for Crew Health and Readiness: tracks crew well-being, activity and sleep (actigraphy) and behavioural-performance surveys before, during and after Artemis II.

astra.how: ASTRA asks for the same things every day: sleep hours, a mood check-in and activity, and compares them with each astronaut's own baseline.

studies.name: Immune Biomarkers
studies.summary: Analyses blood and saliva from the Artemis II crew to see how deep-space travel affects the immune system.

astra.how: ASTRA watches the immune signs a crew can read on board (fever, sore throat, rash) and shows real astronaut white-cell counts from Inspiration4.

studies.name: Artemis II Standard Measures
studies.summary: The Artemis II crew provided a standardized set of health data to a repository for future research.

astra.how: ASTRA's routine collects one standard set of checks at the same times every day, so readings stay comparable across a mission.

studies.name: B-Complex
studies.summary: Tests whether a daily B-vitamin supplement can prevent or reduce eye and brain changes in spaceflight.

astra.how: The weekly Amsler-grid check is how a crew member notices the vision changes this study tries to prevent.

studies.name: Brain Fluid Pressure
studies.summary: Examines how pressure inside the skull relates to eye and brain changes in astronauts.

studies.name: CIPHER
studies.summary: A suite of studies on how many body systems change together during orbital flight.

astra.how: ASTRA's body map shows eight body systems side by side, so changes in several systems are seen together.

studies.name: Simulating Manual Piloting for Moon Landings
studies.summary: Assesses whether moving between gravity levels affects astronauts' manual piloting for lunar landings.

astra.how: The reaction-time tap test gives a quick readiness signal before a demanding task.

studies.name: Spacecraft Occupant Protection
studies.summary: Surveys crew discomfort during re-entry and combines it with spacecraft sensor data.

astra.how: Back pain and other symptoms are logged in the symptom check.

studies.name: Spinal Fluid Biomarkers
studies.summary: Looks for substances in spinal fluid linked to spaceflight-related eye and brain changes.

studies.name: Standard Measures
studies.summary: Collects a consistent set of physiological and psychological measures before, during and after flight: blood, activity and light exposure, sleep, saliva (immune), cognition, balance, strength and microbiome.

astra.how: ASTRA's on-board versions: sleep hours, a reaction-time test for cognition, exercise minutes, dizziness in the symptom check, and real Inspiration4 blood panels.

studies.name: Thigh Cuff
studies.summary: Tests whether tight thigh cuffs keep fluid in the legs and help prevent spaceflight eye problems.

astra.how: Vision self-check; the fluid shift it fights is explained on the eyes card.

studies.name: Venous Haemostasis
studies.summary: Examines differences between astronauts that may change blood flow and clotting in space.

astra.how: Heart rate and blood pressure against each astronaut's own baseline.

studies.name: Zero T2
studies.summary: Studies how exercising without a treadmill affects health and performance ahead of deep-space missions.

astra.how: ASTRA's exercise sessions are equipment-light, the situation Zero T2 prepares for.
